svg.title: Four Labels on One Autonomy Spectrum, Plus One Orthogonal Architecture Choice
svg.desc: A horizontal spectrum runs from low autonomy, where a human approves or performs every action, to high autonomy, where the system runs a multi-step task to completion on its own. Chatbot sits at the low end: conversational text only, answering one request at a time. Assistant sits next: it interprets intent and takes one action per user turn. Copilot sits further along: it can chain several actions together, but is deliberately designed to keep a human closely paired with it, reviewing before anything lands. Agent sits at the high end: the model directs its own multi-step process toward a goal with no fixed sequence and no human reviewing each step. A separate box below states that workflow is not a fifth point on this same spectrum: it describes whether a human-written program fixes the sequence of steps in code, a question about architecture that applies underneath any of the four labels above, independently of how autonomous the resulting system looks from the outside.
svg.text: Four Labels on One Autonomy Spectrum, Plus One Orthogonal Architecture Choice
human does or approves each action
runs multi-step task to completion alone
built to keep a human paired in
Workflow is not a fifth point on this line.
It answers a separate question: does a human-written program fix the sequence of steps in code,
or does the model decide it at runtime? That question applies underneath any of the four labels above.
A chatbot, an assistant, and a copilot are almost always workflows; only an agent can be one or not.
